constraints.text: Request: a fresh token, once a minute, only for an inbox reply
Acknowledge: the right token returns the reply subject and is spent
RejectAck: a wrong or repeated token changes nothing
emitted t <= 1: one channel event per request however often it is delivered
constraints.verifiedBy: the emitter tests check once per request, and the daemon test checks the daemon sends one event per window; neither delivers the same channel_check_request frame to the client twice, which is what the constraint says
constraints.suggestedTest: tests/test_daemon/test_channel_feed.py: publish one CheckRequest, let the feed emit it, make the daemon deliver the same request frame again (a second subscription of the same session, as test_a_new_subscription_gets_the_pending_request_again does at frame level), and assert the client's sink holds exactly one channel_check frame (kinds().count('channel_check') == 1)

constraints.text: relayed t <= 1: the acknowledgement is relayed to the doctor once however often it arrives
constraints.verifiedBy: a real daemon over a push relay: the first ack publishes one CheckAck to the reply subject; a second ack answers 'not accepted' and the published count stays 1; a wrong token publishes nothing. The assertion that would fail if the property broke: 'assert len(rig.acks()) == 1' after a repeated channel_ack in test_a_repeated_acknowledgement_changes_nothing

daemon-sourced half covered by tests/test_daemon/test_channel_feed.py::test_a_channel_check_event_carries_biffds_token_and_the_ack_goes_through: the token of the channel_check frame is the one the daemon issued, shown by 'assert reply["text"] == "biff channel live."' and 'assert [a.token for a in acks] == [token]' (the acknowledged token is the sent token, relayed once). Client half uncovered: no assertion distinguishes 'sent' from 'emitted' in the code, and no test would fail if a second frame were sent for the same token after the first, because the test reads only the first channel_check frame. A worker is writing it (branch tests-channel-check-gaps)
constraints.suggestedTest: tests/test_daemon/test_channel_feed.py: after the acknowledged check, assert kinds().count('channel_check') == 1 and that its token equals the single CheckAck's token

constraints.text: DeliverRequest: at-least-once delivery of the request frame to the session client
constraints.verifiedBy: a pending check is delivered to the first subscription, then a second subscription of the same session receives unread and the same request again, before any acknowledgement; the ack is then relayed once

constraints.text: SendEvent: needs the request to have reached the client
constraints.verifiedBy: read on main afcb2b3. The feed test starts the client's DaemonChannelFeed over a real daemon, publishes a CheckRequest on the bus and waits for a channel_check frame in the client's sink; it then reads the 128-bit token out of that frame and calls channel_ack with it. The assertions that fail if the client sent without the request reaching it: 'await rig.wait_for(lambda: "channel_check" in rig.sink.kinds())' (no frame without the request) and 'assert reply["text"] == "biff channel live."' (the daemon accepts only the token it issued for that request, so a frame with an invented token is refused). The daemon test shows the pending request follows the unread summary. The emitter's 'waits for the client to be initialised' test does not exercise this constraint

constraints.text: DeliverRequest: a request frame replayed after the acknowledgement (afterAck >= 1) makes no second event and no second relayed ack
constraints.verifiedBy: the daemon side is exercised: test_a_request_replayed_after_the_acknowledgement_makes_nothing shows a new subscription gets no second request event and a second channel_ack relays nothing. The constraint is about the client too (a request frame replayed after the ack makes no event and no ack); no test hands the client's feed a replayed request frame after the ack. The daemon half stays as evidence
constraints.suggestedTest: tests/test_daemon/test_channel_feed.py: ack the check, make the feed's subscription reopen (the daemon replays the spent request or the test injects the frame), and assert no second channel_check frame in the sink and no second CheckAck on the bus (len(acks) == 1)
